Welcome to **Algorithms**, a structured, English-language knowledge map covering **all 73 topic labels visible in the LeetCode Problemset on 25 November 2026**.

::: {.callout-note}
## What exactly is covered?

The source is the [official LeetCode Problems topic list](https://leetcode.com/problemset/). Its tags mix **algorithm paradigms** (such as dynamic programming), **data structures** (such as heaps and tries), and **problem domains** (such as database, shell and concurrency). This library preserves all of those names rather than incorrectly calling every tag an algorithm.

These are the visible tags at the stated snapshot date, not an exhaustive list of every named algorithm used in computer science. LeetCode may change its catalogue later.
:::

## A mathematical approach to algorithms

An algorithm can be treated as a state transformation that preserves an invariant and, when it terminates, returns a valid result:

$$
S_{t+1}=F(S_t,x_t),qquad
orall t; I(S_t),qquad
T(n)in Oigl(f(n)igr).
$$

Here $S_t$ denotes algorithm state, $x_t$ the input or decision at step $t$, $F$ the transition rule, $I$ a correctness invariant, and $T(n)$ the runtime as a function of input size $n$. **This is a general study framework**, not a claim that every topic has the same complexity or an online state transition.

For every topic, begin with a concrete problem, define the state and constraints, derive a formal relationship, explain correctness, analyse time/space costs, then implement and test. Different topics need different proof techniques.

## Suggested study order

A practical route starts with arrays, strings and hashing; progresses to two pointers, sliding window, recursion, binary search and backtracking; then covers tree/graph traversals, greedy algorithms and dynamic programming. Finally, explore advanced range queries, graph algorithms, probabilistic techniques and specialised problem domains.

**Choose a problem's strategy by its constraints and structure, not merely its LeetCode tags.** Several different algorithms can solve the same problem.

## Source and maintenance

This taxonomy was checked against the [LeetCode Problemset](https://leetcode.com/problemset/) on **2026-11-25**. The [machine-readable tag catalogue](leetcode-topic-catalog.json) records the exact names, independent folder slugs, topic groupings and short mathematical starting points. The collection can be updated when LeetCode changes its topic list.
